title: What HTTPS still shows
fullTitle: HTTPS Encrypts Your Request. What Can the Network Still See?

scenes.narration: The browser goes to example dot test, slash account, tab equals billing, hash history. The padlock is on. On the path sits a passive observer. This is a conceptual illustration, not a capture. What can that observer still read?
captions: A passive observer sits on the network path. Illustration, not a capture.

scenes.narration: First a name must become an address. With plain DNS the question for example dot test crosses the network unencrypted. Whether the observer sees it depends on the transport and on where it sits.
captions: Plain DNS: the question for example.test is unencrypted.
Visibility depends on DNS transport and observer position.

scenes.narration: Then the connection itself. Destination address, port four four three, when packets flow and how large they are. All visible. An address alone does not necessarily identify one website.
captions: Destination IP, port 443, timing and volume are visible.
An IP address does not necessarily identify one unique website.

scenes.narration: The TLS ClientHello goes first, in plaintext. Without Encrypted Client Hello it names the server. Example dot test, again.
captions: ClientHello is plaintext. No ECH: the SNI names example.test.

scenes.narration: The ServerHello answers, both sides derive keys, and from this point the handshake itself is encrypted.
captions: ServerHello: keys agreed. The rest of the handshake is encrypted.

scenes.narration: In TLS one point three the server certificate travels inside that encrypted handshake. The observer sees ciphertext and a length, not the certificate.
captions: TLS 1.3: the server certificate is inside the encrypted handshake.
The observer sees a record length, not the certificate.

scenes.narration: Then the request. Method, path, query, headers, cookies, body: all encrypted application data. Only record sizes and timing leak, and those alone do not reveal the exact content.
captions: Record sizes and timing leak, but not the exact content by themselves.

scenes.narration: Both ends hold plaintext. The browser built the request; the terminating server decrypts it and may log it. If a CDN terminates TLS, the CDN is that endpoint. And the fragment, hash history, never left the browser.
captions: Browser and TLS endpoint both hold the plaintext. The server may log it.
The fragment #history never left the browser.

scenes.narration: Encrypted content can still travel with visible metadata. Encrypted DNS hides the question, not the address. ECH hides the name in the hello, not everything. And HTTPS does not stop phishing or a compromised endpoint.
captions: Encrypted content can still travel with visible metadata.
Encrypted DNS hides the question, not the IP. ECH hides the SNI, not everything.
